summary: Eleven comment-endorsed tools, apps, books and creative resources from the complete HN front-page crawl.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Floci
items.source_story_title: Floci: Locally emulating any cloud service
items.summary: A local cloud-service emulator praised for lightweight integration testing with Testcontainers.
items.why_included: A developer reports sustained use and explicitly praises its lightweight testing workflow.
items.evidence: A user says Floci has worked well for integration tests and is lighter than LocalStack.

evidence_sources.author: microflash
evidence_sources.excerpt: Been using it for a while to run integration tests with Testcontainers [1]. It's very good and much more lightweight than Localstack.

items.name: grill-me
items.summary: An agent skill that interviews you about implementation choices before coding begins.
items.why_included: A developer reports a marked improvement in implementation quality from using the questioning skill.
items.evidence: A user says the simple interviewing skill made Claude's implementation quality feel substantially better.

evidence_sources.author: valzam
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have been using this super simple skill[0] to make Claude ask exhaustive questions about the implementation of larger features. It has been absolutely amazing and felt like a step change in the output quality.

items.name: Schematic
items.source_story_title: Is your Postgres migration safe or not safe?
items.summary: A database schema-management tool that avoids routine migrations for additive changes.
items.why_included: A production user credits it with avoiding routine migration work and guarding destructive changes.
items.evidence: A user says Schematic handles most additive changes without migrations and refuses potentially destructive auto-generated migrations.

evidence_sources.author: agubelu
evidence_sources.excerpt: the tool we use for schema management [1] removes the need for migrations for most additive schema changes. It refuses to auto-generate potentially destructive migrations

items.name: vercel-labs/emulate
items.source_story_title: Floci: Locally emulating any cloud service
items.summary: An extensible service-emulation framework used to model cloud integrations and hardware devices.
items.why_included: A developer reports successful custom emulators and praises its working foundation.
items.evidence: A developer describes successful custom emulators and calls the project's existing framework a useful base.

evidence_sources.author: tough
evidence_sources.excerpt: i've made custom ones for stuff like emulating hardware devices (airplay/google play) with much success

items.name: whiteboard-mcp
items.source_story_title: Drawgent: Coding agent on a live Excalidraw canvas
items.summary: A whiteboard integration for agents creating architecture diagrams.
items.why_included: A commenter reports firsthand success and prefers it to other free diagramming alternatives.
items.evidence: A user reports good results with whiteboard-mcp for architecture diagrams.

items.name: Reladraw
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Reladraw – A diagram language where you decide where to place things
items.summary: A diagram-as-code language that lets authors specify relative placement of elements.
items.why_included: Commenters explicitly praise its approach to controlling diagram layout.
items.evidence: One commenter loves its approach and another says they intend to use it for their diagrams.

evidence_sources.author: kinduff
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love it, and I wish it was part of Mermaid.

evidence_sources.author: ciefa
evidence_sources.excerpt: Definitely going to make use of this, I didn't know how much I wanted something like this until right now hahaha.

items.name: Conversations
items.source_story_title: Breaking Up with Google Play: Why Conversations Is Now Free
items.summary: An Android XMPP messenger that a longtime user relies on for family chats.
items.why_included: A commenter gives unambiguous positive firsthand experience over several years.
items.evidence: A user thanks the developer and says Conversations has been their go-to for friends and family for years.

evidence_sources.author: 4chandaily
evidence_sources.excerpt: thank you for Conversations, Daniel, it has been my go-to for years for communicating with friends and family.

items.name: Hacker Atlas
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Hacker Atlas - A map of what Hacker News talks about
items.summary: A visual map of Hacker News topics with a clean, mobile-friendly interface.
items.why_included: A commenter praises the presentation and bookmarks the project.
items.evidence: A commenter calls its interface clean and mobile-friendly, then bookmarks it.

evidence_sources.author: alfg
evidence_sources.excerpt: Great idea. UI looks good and clean as well as mobile-friendly. Thanks for this, bookmarked.

items.name: Drawesome
items.source_story_title: How to keep enjoying programming in a world of LLMs
items.summary: A collaborative drawing canvas whose creator says their children enjoy it.
items.why_included: Its creator reports specific positive use by the intended family audience.
items.evidence: The maker says their children love sharing the drawing canvas.

evidence_sources.author: kraig911
evidence_sources.excerpt: multiple people drawing/painting/coloring on the same canvas my kids love this.

items.name: mobygratis
items.source_story_title: A searchable library of forgotten public-domain film clips from 1915 onward
items.summary: Moby's free instrumental-music library for filmmakers and other creators.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly suggests it to found-footage makers and praises its collection.
items.evidence: A commenter calls mobygratis an amazing gift to filmmakers and a pleasant listening library.

evidence_sources.author: ynac
evidence_sources.excerpt: an amazing gift to filmmakers and a pretty snazzy listening experience for (semi-)library music.

items.name: Sacred Economics
items.source_story_title: Breaking Up with Google Play: Why Conversations Is Now Free
items.summary: Charles Eisenstein's freely readable book about money, gift economies and exchange.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommends the book in the discussion of platform economics.
items.evidence: A commenter recommends Sacred Economics as related reading and notes it is free online.

evidence_sources.author: N_Lens
evidence_sources.excerpt: I recommend the book “sacred economics” regarding this play. Free to read online
